title: Nick's piano and fans such as Ted Husing and Charles Edward Smith
summary: Nick played piano on tuned uprights at the club, and Husing, Billy Hill and Charles Edward Smith were fans.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did Nick ever play with the band much?

Oh yeah, Nick played piano, you see. And he had two pianos on the stand for that purpose, so he could come and sit in and play. And if he'd look at the keys, he'd miss, he couldn't play, he'd have to look up at the ceiling while he played. And he'd look up at the ceiling and just keep playing, boy, and he'd get a tremendous kick out of that. And Ted Husing used to come in quite a while, quite a bit every so often, maybe two, three times a week. And Billy Hill, the old songwriter that did, the one who wrote the Last Roundup and Old Spinning Wheel and those things, he was quite a fan of ours.
Now Nick, was the piano playing on the nightclub? I can't understand that. You mean the piano was in tune?
Yes, he kept two pianos on the stand. One was for him to play on. Two uprights.
Was that the only job he ever played where the piano was in tune? Yeah.
Oh yeah, well he kept them in tune purposely, you know.
That's something that's really awful here, you know.

You probably know, it's Paul Edouard Smith, or is it Edouard Smith? Charles Edouard. Charles Edouard Smith, yeah. He was quite a fan of ours and when I came back home, he came back all the way down to New Orleans to hear me play again, he told me. He liked my little register so much. He had some job for the government, wasn't it in Washington?
He was writing for the Department of Agriculture.
He's still going strong, still writing in New Orleans. He is? He's got things in several books out now. Of course he's an editor of that Jazzman, which I thought was a good book for its time.
